Catch Me If You Can is a 2002 crime comedy-drama directed by Steven Spielberg and based on the real-life exploits of teenage con artist Frank Abagnale Jr. Leonardo DiCaprio stars as Frank, a charismatic high-schooler whose parents’ divorce and his father’s financial troubles send him running away with little more than a checkbook. He quickly discovers a talent for forgery and impersonation, cashing millions in fake checks while posing as a Pan Am pilot, a pediatrician, and a lawyer. Tom Hanks plays the dogged FBI agent Carl Hanratty, whose years-long pursuit of Frank becomes a cat-and-mouse game that stretches across the United States and Europe. The film balances lighthearted caper energy with the emotional fallout of a fractured family, showing how Frank’s cons serve as both an escape and an attempt to recapture the stability he lost.

Spielberg’s polished, 1960s-period production features a memorable John Williams score and strong supporting turns from Christopher Walken as Frank’s charming but failing father and Amy Adams as the nurse Frank falls for. Made on a $52 million budget, the movie opened on Christmas Day 2002 and went on to earn more than $352 million worldwide. Critics praised DiCaprio’s magnetic performance and the film’s mix of humor and pathos; it earned Academy Award nominations for Walken’s supporting work and Williams’s score, along with several other honors. The story ends on a note of redemption, with Frank later using his expertise to help catch other forgers, turning the same skills that once made him a fugitive into a legitimate career.
